Probability and statistics in 1 minute

Short videos for ES 114 Probability, Statistics and Data Visualization at IIT Gandhinagar: one question per Short, answered in under a minute with a small example, in the same style as Machine learning in 1 minute.

The first Shorts will be listed here once they are published. Until then, the ES 114 course page has the lecture material.

Watch Machine learning in 1 minute ES 114 course page (2025)

Planned questions

39 questions, in course order. Each Short will ask one of them and work out the answer. The list may change as the Shorts are made.

Probability basics

  1. Flip two fair coins. Which is more likely: two heads, or one head and one tail?
  2. A die has 6 faces. How many different events can you ask about ("even", "1 or 5", ...)?
  3. Roll a die 4 times. What is the chance of at least one six?

Counting

  1. 10 people each shake hands once with everyone else. How many handshakes?
  2. 23 people in a room. What is the chance two share a birthday?

Conditional probability and Bayes

  1. You pick door 1 of 3. The host, who knows where the car is, opens door 3: a goat. Switch to door 2?
  2. A test catches 90% of sick people and wrongly flags 5% of healthy ones. 5% of people are sick. You test positive. Chance you are sick?
  3. Same test. You test positive twice (independent tests). Now how likely are you sick?
  4. A fair coin lands heads 5 times in a row. Chance the next flip is heads?
  5. Teacher A has the higher pass rate in both the easy and the hard section. Can teacher B have the higher pass rate overall?

Random variables

  1. Roll two dice and add them. Which total comes up most often?
  2. Roll two dice and keep the bigger one. Which value is most likely?

Common distributions

  1. A box has 10 eggs; each is cracked with chance 10%. Most likely number of cracked eggs?
  2. A help desk gets 6 calls an hour on average. Which is more likely in the next hour: exactly 5 calls or exactly 6?
  3. Roll a die until you get a six. Which number of rolls is most likely?
  4. You round prices to the nearest rupee. On average, how big is the rounding error?
  5. Waits at a counter average 10 minutes (exponential). What share wait less than 10 minutes?
  6. Marks follow a bell curve with average 70 and spread (standard deviation) 8. What share score above 86?
  7. Can a probability density be bigger than 1?
  8. A loaded die shows faces 1 to 4 with chances 0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4. The computer draws u = 0.45. Which face does it show?

Expectation and variance

  1. 10 people's hats are handed back at random. On average, how many get their own hat?
  2. You play 100 fair coin flips, winning or losing Rs 100 each. The average result is 0. How far from 0 do you typically end?
  3. You know only the mean and SD of some data. What share is guaranteed to lie within 2 SDs of the mean?

Joint distributions and correlation

  1. Throw a dart uniformly at a 2 x 2 square. Chance it lands in the circle that just fits inside?
  2. Y is exactly X squared, with X = -2, -1, 0, 1, 2 equally likely. What is their correlation?
  3. On 6 days, ice-cream sales and sunburn cases rise together (correlation 0.99). Does ice cream cause sunburn?
  4. A parcel's weight error is 3 g (SD) on one scale and 4 g on another, independent. SD of the total error?
  5. Students scored 20 above average on test 1. Tests 1 and 2 correlate 0.5 (same spread). Expected test 2 score?

Law of large numbers and central limit theorem

  1. You got 7 heads in 10 flips. After 1,000 more fair flips, the share of heads will be about...
  2. Which is more likely to give 60% or more heads: 10 flips or 100 flips?
  3. One die is flat: every face equally likely. What does the total of 10 dice look like?

Sampling and estimation

  1. Run a random-number generator twice with the same seed. Same numbers?
  2. A poll of 100 people is good to about plus or minus 10 points. How many people for plus or minus 5?
  3. A coin gives 7 heads in 10 flips. Which heads chance makes that most likely: 0.5, 0.7 or 0.9?
  4. A computer multiplies 1,100 chances of 0.5. What does it get?

Data visualization choices

  1. On this chart the new bar looks 3 times taller than the old one. How much did sales grow?
  2. On this chart the line climbs the same height each year. Did it grow by the same amount each year?
  3. Class A scored 66, 68, 70, 72, 74; class B 40, 45, 70, 95, 100. Which has the higher average?
  4. Nine people earn 30,000 and one earns 300,000. What is the average pay?
